source_text: IX. Τῷ δὲ Πολυκάρπῳ εἰσιόντι εἰς τὸ στάδιον φωνὴ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐγένετο· Ἴσχυε, Πολύκαρπε, καὶ ἀνδρίζου. Καὶ τὸν μὲν εἰπόντα οὐδεὶς εἶδεν, τὴν δὲ φωνὴν τῶν ἡμετέρων οἱ παρόντες ἤκουσαν. Καὶ λοιπὸν προσαχθέντος αὐτοῦ θόρυβος ἦν μέγας ἀκουσάντων ὅτι Πολύκαρπος συνείληπται. Προσαχθέντα οὖν αὐτὸν ἀνηρώτα ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἰ αὐτὸς εἴη Πολύκαρπος. Τοῦ δὲ ὁμολογοῦντος, ἔπειθεν ἀρνεῖσθαι λέγων· Αἰδέσθητί σου τὴν ἡλικίαν, καὶ ἕτερα τούτοις ἀκόλουθα, ὡς ἔθος αὐτοῖς λέγειν· Ὄμοσον τὴν Καίσαρος τύχην, μετανόησον· εἶπον· Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους. Ὁ δὲ Πολύκαρπος ἐμβριθὲς τῷ προσώπῳ εἰς πάντα τὸν ὄχλον τὸν ἐν τῷ σταδίῳ ἀνόμων ἐθνῶν ἐμβλέψας καὶ ἐπισείσας αὐτοῖς τὴν χεῖρα, στενάξας τε καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, εἶπεν· Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους. Ἐγκειμένου δὲ τοῦ ἀνθυπάτου καὶ λέγοντος· Ὄμοσον, καὶ ἀπολύω σε· λοιδόρησον τὸν Χριστόν, ἔφη ὁ Πολύκαρπος· Ὀγδοήκοντα καὶ ἓξ ἔτη δουλεύω αὐτῷ, καὶ οὐδέν με ἠδίκησεν· καὶ πῶς δύναμαι βλασφημῆσαι τὸν βασιλέα μου, τὸν σώσαντά με;
thought_title: Polycarp turns the insult back and refuses to revile Christ
orientation: Polycarp has been led into the crowded stadium and the proconsul is now questioning him and urging him to swear by Caesar and deny being a Christian.
pass_a_gloss: But as Polycarp was entering into the stadium, a voice from heaven came: Be strong, Polycarp, and act as a man. And no one saw the one who had spoken, but those of our people who were present heard the voice. And then when he was brought forward there was a great uproar, when they heard that Polycarp had been seized. So when he had been brought forward, the proconsul questioned him whether he himself was Polycarp. And when he confessed it, he kept urging him to deny, saying: Respect your age, and other things following after these, as is the custom for them to say: Swear by the fortune of Caesar, change your mind; say: Away with the godless people. But Polycarp, looking with a stern face upon all the crowd of lawless nations in the stadium and waving his hand at them, and groaning and looking up into heaven, said: Away with the godless people. But as the proconsul pressed hard and said: Swear, and I release you; revile Christ, Polycarp said: Eighty-six years I serve him, and he wronged me in nothing; and how am I able to speak evil against my king, the one who saved me?

lemmas.gloss: act as a man, be courageous

choices.english: Be strong, Polycarp, and act as a man
choices.why: keeps both imperatives and their distinct force instead of merging into one encouragement
literal rendering of τύχη as fortune, the oath formula demanded
keeps imperative exclamation and uses brief glossary English for ἄθεοι
keeps the two different Greek verbs distinct, command then Polycarp's refusal

pass_b_english: As Polycarp entered the stadium, a voice came from heaven saying, "Be strong, Polycarp, and act as a man." No one saw the one who spoke, but those of our people who were present heard the voice.

After he was brought forward, a great uproar broke out when people heard that Polycarp had been arrested. When he was led up, the proconsul asked him if he himself was Polycarp. When he confessed that he was, the proconsul urged him to deny, saying, "Respect your age," along with the other things they customarily say: "Swear by the fortune of Caesar, repent, say, 'Away with the godless people.'"

Polycarp looked with a stern face at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium, waved his hand toward them, groaned and looked up to heaven, and said, "Away with the godless people." As the proconsul kept pressing him and saying, "Swear, and I will set you free; revile Christ," Polycarp said, "For eighty-six years I have served him, and he never did me any wrong. How can I speak evil against my king who saved me?"

last_rejected.quote: the proconsul urged him to deny, saying, "Respect your age," along with the other things they customarily say: "Swear by the fortune of Caesar, repent, say, 'Away with the godless people.'"
last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς ἔθος αὐτοῖς λέγειν· Ὄμοσον τὴν Καίσαρος τύχην, μετανόησον· εἶπον· Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους.
last_rejected.why: The source marks "Away with the godless people" as the crowd's shout (εἶπον), separate from the proconsul's urging. The English folds the crowd's cry into the proconsul's speech, blurring whose words these are.
last_rejected.fix: the proconsul urged him to deny, saying, "Respect your age," along with the other things they customarily say: "Swear by the fortune of Caesar, repent." The crowd shouted, "Away with the godless people."
last_rejected.ruling: εἶπον here is the imperative 'say' (εἰπόν), continuing the proconsul's formula 'Ὄμοσον… μετανόησον· εἶπον· Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους'. The English is correct, not a crowd cry.
